foodMatrices.name: Beef & Red Meat (Steaks, Roasts, Whole Muscle)
foodMatrices.visualProgression: Vibrant cherry red (oxymyoglobin) -> dull purplish-brown (metmyoglobin) -> chalky dry tan leathery patch
foodMatrices.trimmingAdvice: Trim grayish-brown dry rind (1.5–2.5 mm depth) with a chef's knife before cooking. Interior muscle fibers remain juicy and flavorful.
foodMatrices.salvageCookingTechnique: Low-and-slow braising in acidic wine/tomato liquids, beef bourguignon, pot roast, or shredded beef chili. Avoid quick high-heat dry grilling.

foodMatrices.name: Ground Beef & Minced Meat (Burgers, Patties, Bulk)
foodMatrices.visualProgression: Bright red -> mottled brownish-gray throughout interior and exterior due to trapped internal void air
foodMatrices.trimmingAdvice: Trimming impossible due to ground structural dispersion. Desiccated patties cook dry and rubbery with noticeable cardboard notes.
foodMatrices.salvageCookingTechnique: Heavily season and incorporate into bold sauces: spicy taco meat, Texas chili, bolognese, or shepherd's pie with Worcestershire and tomato paste.

foodMatrices.name: Skinless Chicken / Turkey Breast (Poultry Fillets)
foodMatrices.visualProgression: Translucent pink -> opaque chalky white dry patches resembling bleached cardboard
foodMatrices.trimmingAdvice: Shave off white desiccated patches (1–2 mm depth). Underneath, meat color returns to normal translucent pink.
foodMatrices.salvageCookingTechnique: Poach gently in aromatics or simmer in chicken soup, then shred finely for buffalo chicken dip, enchiladas, or pot pie.

foodMatrices.name: Whole Chicken / Bone-In Thighs (Skin-On Poultry)
foodMatrices.visualProgression: Supple creamy-yellow skin -> parchment-like brittle dry skin with yellowish-brown edge curling
foodMatrices.trimmingAdvice: Strip and completely discard freezer-burned skin; skin fat concentrates malondialdehyde and lipid rancidity. Muscle underneath is well-protected.
foodMatrices.salvageCookingTechnique: Braise skinless thighs in curry, Moroccan tagine, or coq au vin with hearty root vegetables.

foodMatrices.name: Fatty Salmon, Trout & Mackerel Fillets
foodMatrices.visualProgression: Deep coral-orange with moist sheen -> dull opaque brownish-yellow, dry crystalline glaze, oily rancid odor
foodMatrices.trimmingAdvice: Trim desiccated outer perimeter and scrape away the dark brownish lateral bloodline fat where rancid lipid peroxides concentrate.
foodMatrices.salvageCookingTechnique: Flake into salmon patties or fish cakes with lemon juice, fresh dill, dijon mustard, and capers to neutralize hexanal aldehydes.

foodMatrices.name: Lean White Fish (Cod, Haddock, Halibut, Tilapia)
foodMatrices.visualProgression: Pearly translucent white -> dry, fibrous, chalky white with cotton-wool spongy texture upon thawing
foodMatrices.trimmingAdvice: Shave dry edges with a sharp knife. If desiccation exceeds 30%, fish will be rubbery and water will purge upon cooking.
foodMatrices.salvageCookingTechnique: Beer-batter fry for fish tacos or simmer in creamy fish chowder with potatoes and cream to restore lost lipid mouthfeel.

foodMatrices.name: Pork Chops & Pork Tenderloin
foodMatrices.visualProgression: Rosy pale pink -> pale beige-white dry leathery patches around perimeter fat cap
foodMatrices.trimmingAdvice: Cut away dried white edges (1.5 mm). Trim the outer fat cap if it has turned yellow from oxidation.
foodMatrices.salvageCookingTechnique: Slow-braise with apples, cider, and grain mustard, or shred into carnitas with Mexican spices and citrus juice.

foodMatrices.name: Frozen Blanched Vegetables (Broccoli, Peas, Corn, Beans)
foodMatrices.visualProgression: Vibrant emerald green -> dull faded brownish-olive, encased in coarse ice crystal matrix
foodMatrices.trimmingAdvice: Rinse off surface frost quickly in a colander under cold water to prevent ice crystal water from diluting cooked dishes.
foodMatrices.salvageCookingTechnique: Do not steam or saute (will be limp and mushy). Puree into cream of broccoli or vegetable bisque, or bake into cheesy casseroles.

foodMatrices.name: Artisan Bread, Rolls & Bagels
foodMatrices.visualProgression: Elastic tender crumb -> brittle, chalky white patches of retrograded desiccated starch
foodMatrices.trimmingAdvice: No trimming needed. Bread simply undergoes extreme retrogradation and surface desiccation.
foodMatrices.salvageCookingTechnique: Slice into homemade garlic-herb croutons, whiz into seasoned dry breadcrumbs in food processor, or bake into savory strata.

foodMatrices.name: Premium Ice Cream & Gelato (Opened Tub)
foodMatrices.visualProgression: Velvety smooth emulsion -> crunchy ice crystal layer on surface, condensed gummy yellow fat layer beneath
foodMatrices.trimmingAdvice: Scrape off top 5–10 mm icy crust with an ice cream paddle and discard.
foodMatrices.salvageCookingTechnique: Blend remaining ice cream into thick milkshakes, milk coffee frappés, or pour over hot brownies.

packagingTypes.name: Commercial Vacuum Seal (3–5 mil EVOH / Multi-Layer Nylon)
packagingTypes.description: Zero internal headspace air. Impermeable barrier halts sublimative water vapor migration and stops atmospheric oxygen dead in its tracks.

packagingTypes.name: Heavy-Duty Freezer Ziploc (Double Seal, Air Manually Expelled)
packagingTypes.description: Thick polyethylene film provides strong moisture containment. Minor air pockets allow slight surface desiccation after 6+ months.

packagingTypes.name: Heavy-Duty Aluminum Foil (Double Wrapped & Crimped Tightly)
packagingTypes.description: True zero-transmission barrier against light, oxygen, and vapor. Requires tight fold crimping to prevent corner air leaks.

packagingTypes.name: Supermarket Styrofoam Tray + Thin PVC Stretch Wrap (Store Pack)
packagingTypes.description: Engineered strictly for 48-hour refrigerated retail cases, NOT freezing. Thin wrap is highly permeable, triggering rapid freezer burn in 3–4 weeks.

packagingTypes.name: Rigid Plastic Container (Snap-Lock Lid with Air Headspace)
packagingTypes.description: The rigid walls prevent moisture escaping outside, but internal water sublimates from food and condenses into heavy frost crystals on lid and container walls.

packagingTypes.name: Unwrapped / Torn Bag / Folded Open Plastic Wrap
packagingTypes.description: Catastrophic exposure. Sublimation proceeds unhindered as dry freezer airflow continuously strips surface moisture, rapidly turning meat into dry leather.

freezerEnvironments.name: Manual Defrost Deep Chest Freezer (-20°F / -29°C)
freezerEnvironments.description: Sub-zero deep cold with zero heating cycles. Ice crystal vapor pressure is extremely low, virtually arresting sublimation and ice recrystallization.

freezerEnvironments.name: Standard Manual Defrost Freezer (0°F / -18°C)
freezerEnvironments.description: USDA recommended baseline freezing condition. Ice sublimates at predictable baseline rates in properly wrapped packaging.

freezerEnvironments.name: Frost-Free / Auto-Defrost Upright Freezer (Cycles up to 25°F / -4°C)
freezerEnvironments.description: Heating coils activate multiple times daily to melt frost off evaporator coils. Repeated warm swings force water to sublimate out of food, causing heavy snow inside packaging.

freezerEnvironments.name: Overloaded / Warm Refrigerator Freezer (+10°F to +15°F / -10°C)
freezerEnvironments.thermalCycleRangeF: Frequent warm spikes due to door openings
freezerEnvironments.description: Warmer temperatures accelerate both chemical enzymatic reactions and lipid peroxidation kinetics, causing food to degrade 3x faster than at 0°F.

scientificBenchmarks.clinicalImpact: Drives continuous moisture migration from warm food interior toward cold freezer surfaces.
Threshold where human sensory panels reliably detect 'cardboard', 'metallic', or 'stale paint' rancidity off-flavors.

scientificBenchmarks.value: Up to 3.8x increase in shear toughness
scientificBenchmarks.clinicalImpact: Desiccated muscle fibers lose their water-binding hydration envelope, resulting in irreversible leathery chewing texture.
Zero microbial growth (Salmonella, E. coli, Listeria) occurs. Freezer-burned meat is 100% microbiologically safe to eat.
